newsitem.title: USA: Chicago eyes bonds for tax increment finance area.
newsitem.headline: Chicago eyes bonds for tax increment finance area.

text.p: Chicago may sell $60 million to $80 million of tax increment finance bonds as part of proposed expansion of a downtown TIF district, a city official said Tuesday.

Walter Knorr, Chicago's chief financial officer, said the administration of Mayor Richard Daley will propose a financing plan for the expanded district at the city council's March meeting. He said the plan will probably contain some bond issuance backed by the incremental increase in property tax revenues within the district.
Mesirow Financial has been tapped to handle the financing, Knorr added.
On Monday, the city council finance committee approved a $300 million redevelopment plan that expands an existing North Loop TIF district by 139 acres.
That plan now heads to the full city council on Friday for final consideration.

Knorr said the expanded TIF district is expected to generate an annual cash flow of $30 million. However, he pointed out that the life of the TIF district would not be extended under the plan and is scheduled to expire in about 10 years.
Revenues from the district and the bond issuance would be used for land acquisition, demolition, rehabilitation and public infrastructure improvements, according to Knorr.
